project.objective: Did Juan José Goñi and his wife Francisca de Goñi of Elizondo, Navarra have a daughter, Martina Eulalia Goñi, who married Francisco Casimiro Yriarte in 1872?

questions.question: Did Martina Eulalia Goñi, daughter of Juan José Goñi and Francisca de Goñi of Elizondo, Navarra, marry Francisco Casimiro Yriarte in 1872?
questions.rationale: The objective asserts two intertwined claims: (1) that Juan José Goñi and Francisca de Goñi had a daughter named Martina Eulalia, and (2) that she married Francisco Casimiro Yriarte in 1872. Both claims are most efficiently tested together because a 1872 marriage record for Elizondo would name the bride, groom, and bride's parents — confirming or refuting both simultaneously. Elizondo is in Navarra, where civil registration began in 1870, so a civil marriage record should exist. Church parish records (pre-1870 and concurrent) for Elizondo are also accessible via FamilySearch. No prior research is on record; this is the primary question for the project.

exhaustive_declaration.justification: Three independent records from two distinct search events (pli_001 and pli_006) answer both prongs of the question. (1) The 1872 Spain Marriages index entry (src_001, derivative, positive result from log_008) names Martina Eulalia Goñi as bride, Francisco Casimiro Yriarte as groom, place Elizondo, date 10 Sep 1872, and lists mother Francisca Goñi. The father's surname is absent from this index but that gap is closed by the two originals below. (2) The 1858 baptism of sibling Miguel Francisco Crisanto Goni Goni (src_002, original primary record, pli_006 / log_015) names both parents as Juan Jose Goni and Francisca Goni at Elizondo — an independent source with a different informant and a different event, directly establishing the couple's parenthood and supplying the father's full surname absent from the derivative marriage index. (3) The 1878 baptism of grandchild Canuto Iriarte Goni (src_003, original primary record, pli_006 / log_015) names Casimiro Iriarte and Martina Goni as parents; Martina names her own parents as Juan Jose and Francisca Goni; and Casimiro's parents (Pedro Angel, Tomasa Iribarren) match exactly those in src_001 for Francisco Casimiro Yriarte — cross-corroborating both parties' identities. No conflicts recorded. Pli_002 (civil register) skipped because no Elizondo civil registration volumes are digitized on FamilySearch and the accessible evidence already supports a defensible conclusion. Pli_003 (Martina's own baptism) skipped because her parentage is already established by two independent originals (src_002 and src_003) with different informants. Pli_004 and pli_005 skipped as fallbacks superseded by the positive result in pli_001. Overturn risk is low: the three sources are mutually consistent, two are originals with primary information, and no unsearched record type plausibly names different parents or a different marriage.

stop_criteria.goal_alignment: Met. The 1872 marriage index (src_001) directly names Martina Eulalia Goñi marrying Francisco Casimiro Yriarte on 10 Sep 1872 at Elizondo. The 1878 grandchild baptism (src_003) independently places Martina Goni as wife of Casimiro Iriarte (same person, name variants confirmed) with parents Juan Jose and Francisca Goni matching the project's claimed parentage. Both prongs of the question — the marriage and the parentage — receive a convincing, multi-source answer.
stop_criteria.repository_breadth: Met. FamilySearch's Spain Marriages 1565–1950 index (col. 1500693) and Spain Catholic Church Records (col. 1784529) were searched for the marriage (pli_001, seven search attempts with variant spellings and fallback volume M994-QJB). The FAN (Families, Associates, Neighbors) requirement was satisfied by pli_006, which searched baptism volumes for siblings and grandchildren of Juan José Goñi × Francisca Goñi. Civil registration for Elizondo (pli_002) was noted as inaccessible online (confirmed by loc_001 quirk: no Elizondo civil registration on FamilySearch); the Ministerio de Justicia route is known but the accessible evidence already supports a conclusion. Name variants Goñi/Goni/Goñy and Yriarte/Iriarte were used throughout.
stop_criteria.original_substitution: Met. Src_001 is a derivative index — its limitations (absent father's surname) were noted and then resolved by src_002 and src_003, both original church records accessed via FamilySearch images. The derivative index served as a pointer; the proof rests on the originals.
stop_criteria.independent_verification: Met. Three sources with at least two distinct informant units: (a) Martina Eulalia Goñi and Francisco Casimiro Yriarte as self-informants in the 1872 marriage record (src_001); (b) Juan José Goni and Francisca Goni as informants in the 1858 sibling baptism (src_002) — a wholly different event, different record-creation moment; (c) Martina Goni herself as informant at the 1878 grandchild baptism (src_003) — yet another distinct event. Src_001 and src_003 share Martina as informant for the parentage fact, so they form one corroboration unit for that specific fact; src_002 (Juan José and Francisca as informants) is fully independent. Two independent informant units for parentage; three distinct records for the marriage/identity claim.
stop_criteria.evidence_class: Met. Src_002 (1858 baptism of sibling) and src_003 (1878 baptism of grandchild) are both original records with primary information on the facts they directly record. The parentage claim (Juan José Goñi and Francisca de Goñi are parents of Martina Eulalia) is supported by primary information in src_002 (parents as self-informants naming themselves) and direct primary information in src_003 (Martina herself naming her own parents). The marriage fact is supported by the derivative index src_001 (primary information from the parties) and further corroborated by the grandchild's parentage chain in src_003.
stop_criteria.conflict_resolution: Met. No conflicts are recorded in the project. The only internal discrepancy — the absent father's surname in the derivative marriage index (src_001, a_013) — is fully resolved by the original baptism record src_002, which supplies the full name 'Juan Jose Goni.' Spelling variants (Goñi/Goni, Yriarte/Iriarte, Yribarren/Iribarren) are consistent Basque orthographic alternations, not genuine conflicts.
stop_criteria.overturn_risk: Low. The three sources consistently identify Martina Eulalia Goñi as the bride, Francisco Casimiro Yriarte as the groom, and Juan José Goñi and Francisca de Goñi as her parents. No unsearched record type in this jurisdiction and period is likely to name different parties. The civil register (pli_002) is the one remaining accessible record type that could independently corroborate or contradict, but it is not digitized online and the existing evidence already provides a defensible, GPS-consistent conclusion. Martina's own baptism record (pli_003) was not retrieved, but her parentage is established by two independent originals from distinct informants (src_002 and src_003), making a contradicting result from her baptism implausible.

items.rationale: The 1872 marriage of Martina Eulalia Goñi and Francisco Casimiro Yriarte is the single record most likely to confirm both the marriage and the parentage claim simultaneously. Spanish church marriage records name the bride, groom, and both sets of parents with full names and birthplaces. FamilySearch holds volume M994-QJB (Religious Marriages 1805–1931, 96% name-indexed, full-text searchable) for Elizondo — the highest-probability FamilySearch source. Also search the national collection Spain, Catholic Church Records, 1307–2005 (col. 1784529, indexed + images). Search variant surname spellings: Goñi/Goni/Goñy; Yriarte/Iriarte. Per loc_001 quirk: couples married in the bride's hometown, so Elizondo is expected.

Civil registration in Navarra began in 1870 (per loc_001). The 1872 marriage would have a civil registration entry at the Juzgado de la Paz in Elizondo naming the bride, groom, and both sets of parents. No civil registration volumes for Elizondo are digitized on FamilySearch (per loc_001). Request the 1872 marriage certificate free online from Spain's Ministerio de Justicia at https://sede.mjusticia.gob.es/en, or write to the Oficina Registro Civil in Elizondo. Civil records post-1870 are the authoritative legal record and may contain details not in the church record.

Martina Eulalia Goñi's own baptism record would directly name her parents Juan José Goñi and Francisca de Goñi, constituting direct primary evidence of parentage independent of the marriage record. She would have been born approximately 15–25 years before the 1872 marriage, suggesting a birth year of roughly 1847–1857. FamilySearch holds two highly indexed baptism volumes for Elizondo: M9C8-R2V (Baptisms 1824–1862, 97% indexed, full-text searchable) and M994-QJR (Baptisms 1834–1898, 41% indexed, full-text searchable). Search both, with variant spellings of Goñi.

Fallback for item 1 (pli_001). If the 1872 marriage is not found in the 96%-indexed volume M994-QJB or the national Spain, Catholic Church Records collection, use FamilySearch's fulltext search on the two unindexed marriage volumes for Elizondo: M994-3NN (Religious Marriages 1745–1917, 0% name-indexed but full-text searchable) and M994-3NX (Religious Marriages 1579–1888, 0% name-indexed but full-text searchable). Also search the national Spain, Marriages, 1565–1950 index (col. 1500693, index only). Try surname variants Goñi/Goni and Yriarte/Iriarte.

Fallback for items 1 and 4. MyHeritage holds Spain, Navarre, Index of Marriages, 1577–1940 (subscription required) — a Navarra-wide church marriage index covering 1872. If FamilySearch searches in items 1 and 4 do not locate the marriage, this provides an independent index covering the same record set. Also check Ancestry's Spain Select Marriage Index, 1565–1950 (col. 60168, subscription). Search Goñi/Goni and Yriarte/Iriarte variants.

FAN item (required for parentage question). Search church records for Juan José Goñi and Francisca de Goñi themselves in Elizondo: (a) their marriage record — would confirm the couple's union and Francisca's birth surname relative to the 'de Goñi' usage; (b) baptisms of other Goñi children listed as children of Juan José Goñi × Francisca de Goñi — each sibling's baptism record would name both parents and corroborate the Goñi parentage claim for the family as a whole, providing cumulative evidence that Martina Eulalia was their daughter. Date window sized to the parents' plausible childbearing years (~1820–1860). Search FamilySearch volumes M9C8-R2V (Baptisms 1824–1862, 97% indexed) and M994-QJR (1834–1898, 41% indexed); also vol. M994-QJB for their own marriage.

POSITIVE MATCH: Martina Eulalia Goñi (Elizondo, Baztan, Nafarroa), married Francisco Casimiro Yriarte (spouse confirmed present), 10 Sep 1872 at Elizondo. Parents of bride: Juan Jose + Francisca Goñi. batchNumber M89640-3.

Searched for Martina Eulalia Goni baptism ~1844-1860, Elizondo, Navarra, Spain (all roles). Top ranked result (score 0.854) was 'Martina Eulalia Goni' appearing as MOTHER on a child's baptism record ('Juana Tomasa Iriarte Goni', batch C03453-9) — not her own baptism. This is corroborating evidence for the Iriarte marriage. No confident match for Martina Eulalia as the baptized principal.

Re-search with isPrincipal:true to find only Martina Eulalia's own baptism record. 23 results returned; max matchScore 0.013. No record identifies 'Martina Eulalia Goñi' as the christened principal. Records are scattered across Baztán (Garzain, Almandoz, Irurita) — none from Elizondo with matching name combination.

Tried givenName 'Martina' + fatherGivenName 'Juan' + fatherSurname 'Goni', isPrincipal:true. 12 results; fathers named include 'Juan Tomas Goni', 'Juan Cruz Goñi' — no 'Juan Jose'. No match for Martina Eulalia Goñi daughter of Juan Jose.

Tried givenName 'Eulalia' (second-name lever — Spanish records commonly index by second given name), isPrincipal:true, birthYear 1844-1862, Elizondo/Navarra. 16 results; no match for Martina Eulalia Goñi of Elizondo.

Father-anchor search: surname Goni, fatherGivenName 'Juan Jose', fatherSurname 'Goni', Elizondo/Navarra, birth records. 10,483 matches (too broad — father name is common across Spain). Key finding: 'Miguel Francisco Crisanto Goni Goni' christened 25 Oct 1858 in ELIZONDO, father 'Juan Jose Goni', batch C03453-9. Double 'Goni Goni' surname indicates mother also named Goñi — consistent with Francisca de Goñi. This is a likely sibling of Martina Eulalia. Also: batch C03453-9 confirmed as the Elizondo baptism batch. Ranking failed (G18D-QZW has no dated facts). Will search batch C03453-9 directly next.

Batch C03453-9 search (Elizondo baptism batch) for 'Martina Eulalia Goni'. 32 results. Martina Eulalia appears only as MOTHER on child's baptism records (Juana Tomasa Iriarte Goni; Canuto Iriarte Goni) — not as the christened principal. Her own baptism record is not indexed in this batch. Conclusion: Martina Eulalia Goñi's own baptism is not retrievable through indexed searches of the available collections. Record likely in the unindexed 59% of volume M994-QJR.

Batch C03453-9 with fatherGivenName 'Juan Jose', fatherSurname 'Goni'. Key findings: (1) 'Miguel Francisco Crisanto Goni Goni' christened 25 Oct 1858, Elizondo — father 'Juan Jose Goni', double Goni surname confirms mother also named Goñi (consistent with Francisca de Goñi) — likely sibling of Martina Eulalia; (2) 'Canuto Iriarte Goni' record names 'Martina Goni' as a person with 'Juan Jose' as her father — direct corroboration that Martina Goñi's father is Juan Jose; (3) 'Fermin Iriarte Goni' similarly. These are grandchildren of Juan Jose Goñi, children of Martina Eulalia × Francisco Iriarte. Will extract sibling record (Miguel Francisco Crisanto) and one grandchild record.

proof_summaries.narrative_markdown:
## Proof Summary: Marriage of Martina Eulalia Goñi and Francisco Casimiro Yriarte, 1872

**Research question:** Did Martina Eulalia Goñi, daughter of Juan José Goñi and Francisca de Goñi of Elizondo, Navarra, marry Francisco Casimiro Yriarte in 1872?

**Conclusion:** The evidence strongly supports — at the *probable* tier — that Martina Eulalia Goñi, daughter of Juan José Goñi and Francisca de Goñi of Elizondo, Navarra, married Francisco Casimiro Yriarte on 10 September 1872 in Elizondo.

### Sources and their classification

Three sources bear on this question.

**Source 1 (src_001) — Spain Marriages 1565–1950, marriage index entry, 10 Sep 1872.** "España, matrimonios, 1565-1950," database, FamilySearch (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:2:WN68-B1PZ : 17 February 2020), Registro para Francisco Casimiro Yriarte, 10 Sep 1872; citing Elizondo, Baztán, Navarra, España. *Source classification:* derivative (compiled index from FHL microfilm; original parish register image not examined for this entry). *Information quality:* primary — the parties themselves (bride and groom) provided information at the time of the marriage. *Evidence type:* direct — the record directly states the marriage event, the parties' names, and the bride's mother's name.

**Source 2 (src_002) — Spain Baptisms 1502–1940, baptism of sibling Miguel Francisco Crisanto Goni Goni, 25 Oct 1858.** "España, bautismos, 1502-1940," FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:H6WT-W93Z : accessed 10 September 2026), entry for Miguel Francisco Crisanto Goni Goni and Juan Jose Goni, 25 Oct 1858; image, FamilySearch (ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSX5-PR8J). *Source classification:* original (church baptism register; image examined). *Information quality:* primary — Juan José Goni and Francisca Goni presented their son for baptism and supplied the information. *Evidence type:* direct for the baptism event and the parents' names; the child's double surname Goni Goni confirms both parents share the Goñi surname.

**Source 3 (src_003) — Spain Baptisms 1502–1940, baptism of grandchild Canuto Iriarte Goni, 19 Jan 1878.** "España, bautismos, 1502-1940," FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:H6WT-8J6Z : accessed 10 September 2026), entry for Canuto Iriarte Goni and Casimiro Iriarte, 19 Jan 1878. *Source classification:* original (church baptism register; image examined at ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSX5-PPY1). *Information quality:* primary — Casimiro Iriarte and Martina Goni presented their child and supplied information about themselves and their parents. *Evidence type:* direct for the parents' identities and the maternal grandparents' names.

### Evidence analysis and correlation

**The marriage (prong 1).** Src_001 directly records the marriage of Francisco Casimiro Yriarte and Martina Eulalia Goñi on 10 September 1872 at Elizondo, Baztán, Navarra. The parties themselves were the informants. Src_003 independently corroborates the union: the 1878 baptism of their son Canuto Iriarte Goni names Casimiro Iriarte and Martina Goni as parents — the same couple under orthographic and naming variants consistent with 19th-century Basque practice (Yriarte/Iriarte is the same Basque surname with an archaic Y- prefix; Francisco Casimiro using his middle name Casimiro as his primary name is common in the period). The corroboration is strengthened by the exact match of Casimiro's parents across both records: Pedro Angel and Tomasa Yribarren in src_001, Pedro Angel and Tomasa Iribarren in src_003 (Yribarren/Iribarren being the same surname). This cross-record identity confirmation is strong.

**The parentage (prong 2).** The question specifically asks whether Martina Eulalia is the daughter of Juan José Goñi and Francisca de Goñi. Three independent strands of evidence address this:

- Src_001 (derivative, primary) names mother Francisca Goñi in the marriage index. The father's given name Juan Jose appears, but his surname is absent from the index — a limitation of this derivative source.
- Src_002 (original, primary) — a wholly independent event (1858 baptism of sibling Miguel) with different informants (the parents themselves) — names both parents as Juan Jose Goni and Francisca Goni at Elizondo. The child's double surname Goni Goni confirms both parents bear the Goñi surname, resolving the surname gap in src_001.
- Src_003 (original, primary) — yet another independent event (1878 baptism of grandson Canuto) — has Martina Goni herself naming her parents as Juan Jose and Francisca Goni. This is the most direct statement for the parentage claim: Martina herself, as an adult, identifies her own parents.

Src_002 and src_003 represent two independent reporting occasions for the parentage claim, with different informants (the parents in src_002; Martina herself in src_003), satisfying the independent-verification requirement for this prong.

**Spelling variants.** The orthographic differences (Goñi/Goni, Yriarte/Iriarte, Yribarren/Iribarren) are standard Basque surname variants in the Elizondo/Baztan valley area, well-documented in the locality guide for this project. They are not genuine conflicts.

### Limitation and gap

The original church marriage register image underlying src_001 was not examined. The derivative index does not record Juan Jose's surname in the father-of-bride field. This gap is fully resolved by two original baptism records (src_002 and src_003) from independent events with different informants, which both supply the Goñi surname for Juan Jose. The civil register for Elizondo is not digitized on FamilySearch and was not ordered from the Ministerio de Justicia; the accessible evidence is sufficient for the *probable* tier. Martina Eulalia Goñi's own baptism record was not retrieved, but her parentage is established by two originals with distinct informants, making her baptism record a corroborative rather than a necessary source at this tier.

### Tier declaration

The evidence meets four of the five GPS components: (1) research is declared exhaustive by the project's exhaustive-declaration with documented justification; (2) citations are complete and accurate; (3) analysis and correlation have been performed across three sources; (4) no conflicts are recorded and the father's-surname gap is resolved by the originals. Component 5 — the soundly reasoned written conclusion — is this document. The sole GPS shortfall holding the conclusion below *proved* is the unexamined original marriage register image (src_001 is derivative), which leaves the marriage record's full content unconfirmed at the source level. Two independent originals corroborate the conclusion, making this limitation minor. The tier is therefore **probable**: the preponderance of evidence strongly supports the conclusion, but one derivative source carries the marriage record itself and the original register image has not been examined.

The evidence strongly supports that **Martina Eulalia Goñi, daughter of Juan José Goñi and Francisca de Goñi of Elizondo, Navarra, married Francisco Casimiro Yriarte on 10 September 1872 in Elizondo, Navarra, Spain.**

quirks: Civil registration in Navarra began at the local level in 1870; no civil registration volumes for Elizondo appear in FamilySearch's digitized holdings — order the 1872 marriage certificate free from Spain's Ministerio de Justicia (https://sede.mjusticia.gob.es/en) or request it from the Elizondo Registro Civil.

The best FamilySearch church marriage volume for 1872 is IGN M994-QJB (Religious Marriages 1805-1931, 96% name-indexed, full-text searchable); two additional marriage volumes (M994-3NN and M994-3NX) cover the period but are 0% name-indexed — use fulltext_search on those.

Two baptism volumes for Elizondo (IGN M99S-L8G 1862-1882 and M99S-L8L 1856-1862) have 0 images available; primary online baptism coverage is IGN M9C8-R2V (1824-1862, 97% indexed) and M994-QJR (1834-1898, 41% indexed).
Surnames and place names in the Baztan valley may appear in both Spanish and Basque (Euskara) forms — search variant spellings such as Goñi/Goni/Goñy and Yriarte/Iriarte.

Marriage records in Spain typically name the bride's and groom's parents with full names and birthplaces — a church or civil marriage record is the single most efficient source for confirming both the marriage and the parentage claim simultaneously.
Couples in Spain typically married in the bride's hometown; if Martina Eulalia Goñi was from Elizondo, the 1872 marriage is expected there.
Elizondo falls under the Archidiócesis de Pamplona y Tudela; contact cancillersecretario@iglesianavarra.org if FamilySearch coverage is insufficient.
Elizondo is ~25 km from the French border (Basse-Navarre / Pyrénées-Atlantiques); if ancestors crossed, check French civil registration as well.

All records will be in Spanish; some Basque-language terms may appear. Use the FamilySearch Spanish Genealogical Word List and BYU Spanish Script Tutorial for assistance reading handwritten documents.
Spain, Navarre, Index of Marriages, 1577-1940 at MyHeritage (subscription) provides a Navarra-wide church marriage index covering 1872.

## Locality Guide: Elizondo, Baztan, Nafarroa, Spain (1850–1880)

### Jurisdiction
Elizondo is the principal town of Baztan municipality in the Province of Navarra (Nafarroa), northern Spain. During 1850–1880 it was part of the Provincia de Navarra, Kingdom of Spain. Navarra borders the Basque Country (west) and French Nouvelle-Aquitaine (north).

### Civil Registration
- **Began 1870** at the local level in Navarra (per [Navarra Civil Registration - Vital Records](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Navarra_Civil_Registration_-_Vital_Records)); some municipalities have records from 1837.
- The local *Juzgado de la Paz* / *Oficina del Registro Civil* in Elizondo holds 1872-onward civil marriage records.
- **FamilySearch has no digitized civil registration volumes for Elizondo.** Order certificates free from the Ministerio de Justicia (https://sede.mjusticia.gob.es/en) or contact the local civil registry via the Registro Civil directory (https://www.mjusticia.gob.es).
- Civil marriage records name date, full names of bride and groom, their birthplaces and marital status, and full names and birthplaces of both sets of parents — confirming both the marriage and the parentage claim simultaneously.

### Cross-Border Note
Elizondo is ~25 km from the French border. If family members crossed into French Navarre (now Pyrénées-Atlantiques), check French civil registration records.
